F4_required_source_material: Klatt, D. H. (1976). Linguistic uses of segmental duration in English: Acoustic and perceptual evidence. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 59(5), 1208-1221. DOI 10.1121/1.380986. Measured segmental durations for English -> d_nominal_s.

Crystal, T. H. & House, A. S. (1988). Segmental durations in connected-speech signals: Current results. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 83(4), 1553-1573. DOI 10.1121/1.395911. Six talkers, two ~300-word scripts; reports mean durations and standard deviations for sound CLASSES and for INDIVIDUAL sounds -> d_nominal_s, and per-phone coverage.
For any ARPAbet consonant not covered above: measurements from a forced-aligned singing corpus (Section 17 F4).
F5_required_source_material: A named standard phonotactics reference giving the exhaustive inventory of legal English syllable-onset consonant clusters, mappable one-to-one onto the ARPAbet consonants in fixtures/lexicon/cmudict.symbols.

Candidates identified bibliographically: Roach, P., 'English Phonetics and Phonology: A Practical Course', 4th ed. (Cambridge University Press, 2009), ch. 8; Cruttenden, A., 'Gimson's Pronunciation of English' (Hodder), section 5.5. NEITHER was retrieved, so NEITHER has been used.
title: SOUND
why: SOUND cannot run without d_nominal/d_floor (Section 7 partition) or the legal-onset table (Section 9 syllabification). Section 22 failure #10 makes a duration-table gap a hard error, never a silent default, so no substitute is available.
